## Source
The data would appear to suggest that caffeine may potentially improve short-term recall in sleep-deprived adults. In a sample consisting of 62 volunteers, the caffeine group was found to score roughly 8% higher on the memory task, though it should be noted that the confidence interval was wide. It is possible that the effect might be confounded by habitual caffeine use, which, unfortunately, we did not control for. These findings should be considered preliminary in nature until such time as they are replicated in a larger and more diverse cohort.

## Gold edit
The data suggest that caffeine may improve short-term recall in sleep-deprived adults. Among 62 volunteers, the caffeine group scored roughly 8% higher on the memory task, but the confidence interval was wide. The effect may be confounded by habitual caffeine use, which we did not control for. The findings are preliminary until replicated in a larger, more diverse cohort.
